\subsection*{Secret Sharing --- Sharing: Results}

\begin{definition}[Polynomial characterization of shares]
\lean{TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing}
\statementsource{Sha79}{
  pdf-a76120fbec44-p001-b005,
  pdf-a76120fbec44-p002-b003
}
\statementsource{BGW88}{pdf-b3f55f2a4332-p003-b005}
\statementsource{AL17}{pdf-27f2b3787521-p004-b002}
\label{TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.Shamir.Party, TCSlib.Shamir.label}
Let $F$ be a field, $d$ a natural number, $x\in F$, and $f$ a function from the nonzero
elements of $F$ to $F$. The function $f$ is a sharing of $x$ of degree at most $d$ if
there is a polynomial $p\in F[X]$ of degree less than $d+1$ such that $p(0)=x$ and, at
every nonzero field element $i$, $f(i)=p(i)$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{3}
Let $F$ be a field, let $k>0$, let $\mathrm{sec}\in F$, and let $q$ be a polynomial of
degree less than $k-1$. In the Shamir scheme over $F$ with parameter $k$, the shares
produced from $\mathrm{sec}$ and $q$ constitute a sharing of $\mathrm{sec}$ with degree
bound less than $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of the sharing degree bound]
\lean{TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing.mono}
\label{TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing.mono}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing}
\difficulty{4}
Let $F$ be a field, let $d,e\in\mathbb N$ with $d\le e$, and let $x\in F$ and $f$ be a
function from the nonzero elements of $F$ to $F$. If $f$ shares $x$ using a polynomial
of degree at most $d$, then it shares $x$ using a polynomial of degree at most $e$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Constant sharing]
\lean{TCSlib.Shamir.isSharing_const}
\label{TCSlib.Shamir.isSharing_const}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing}
\difficulty{3}
Let $F$ be a field, let $d$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $c\in F$. The constant
share function that assigns $c$ to every party is a sharing of $c$ with degree bound
less than $d+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Addition of polynomial sharings]
\lean{TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing.add}
\label{TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing.add}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing}
\difficulty{4}
Let $F$ be a field, let $d\in\mathbb N$, and let $x,y\in F$ and $f,g$ be functions from
the nonzero elements of $F$ to $F$. If $f$ shares $x$ using a polynomial of degree at
most $d$ whose value at zero is $x$, and $g$ shares $y$ in the same way, then the
pointwise sum $f+g$ shares $x+y$ using a polynomial of degree at most $d$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $F$ be a field, let $d\in\mathbb N$, and let $x,c\in F$ and $f$ be a function from
the nonzero elements of $F$ to $F$. If $f$ shares $x$ using a polynomial of degree at
most $d$, then the function sending each participant's share to $c$ times that share
shares $cx$ using a polynomial of degree at most $d$.
\end{theorem}

from the nonzero elements of $F$ to $F$. If $f$ shares $x$ using a polynomial of degree
at most $d$ and $g$ shares $y$ using a polynomial of degree at most $e$, then the
pointwise product $fg$ shares $xy$ using a polynomial of degree at most $d+e$.

\begin{theorem}[Sum of sharings]
\lean{TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing.sum}
\label{TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing.sum}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing, TCSlib.Shamir.IsSharing.add, TCSlib.Shamir.Party, TCSlib.Shamir.isSharing_const}
\difficulty{4}
Let $F$ be a field, let $d$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $s$ be a finite set of
indices. For each $i\in s$, suppose a value $v_i\in F$ is shared by a function $h_i$ on
the nonzero elements of $F$, with each share given by evaluating at its party's label a
polynomial of degree less than $d+1$ whose value at zero is $v_i$. Then the function
that assigns to each party the sum of its shares is a sharing of $\sum_{i\in s}v_i$ with
the same degree bound.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Lagrange recombination coefficient]
\lean{TCSlib.Shamir.recombineCoeff}
\label{TCSlib.Shamir.recombineCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.Shamir.Party, TCSlib.Shamir.label}
Let $F$ be a field with decidable equality, let $A$ be a finite set of parties, and let
$i$ be a party. The recombination coefficient of $i$ relative to $A$ is the value at $0$
of the Lagrange basis polynomial for $A$ associated to $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Weighted reconstruction sum]
\lean{TCSlib.Shamir.recombine}
\statementsource{Sha79}{pdf-a76120fbec44-p002-b003}
\label{TCSlib.Shamir.recombine}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.Shamir.Party, TCSlib.Shamir.recombineCoeff}
Let $F$ be a field, let $A$ be a finite set of nonzero elements of $F$, and let $f$
assign an element of $F$ to each member of $A$. The recombined value is the sum over
$i\in A$ of $f(i)$ weighted by the recombination coefficient of $i$ in $A$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{1}
Let $F$ be a field, let $A$ be a finite set of nonzero elements of $F$, and let $f$
assign a field element to each nonzero element of $F$. Recombining the values of $f$
from $A$ equals the value at zero of the polynomial interpolating those values on $A$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Recombination Equals Reconstruction]
\lean{TCSlib.Shamir.recombine_eq_reconstruct}
\label{TCSlib.Shamir.recombine_eq_reconstruct}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.Shamir.Party, TCSlib.Shamir.recombine, TCSlib.Shamir.recombine_eq_eval_interpolate, TCSlib.Shamir.scheme}
\difficulty{1}
Let $F$ be a field, let $k$ be a natural number, let $A$ be a finite set of nonzero
elements of $F$, and let $f$ assign a field element to each nonzero element of $F$.
Recombining the values of $f$ from $A$ equals the reconstruction of those values by the
scheme that shares a secret using a polynomial $s+Xq(X)$ with $\deg q<k-1$ and
reconstructs by interpolation at zero.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $F$ be a field in which equality is decidable, let $d\in\mathbb N$, and let $x\in F$
and $f$ be a function from the nonzero elements of $F$ to $F$. If $f$ shares $x$ using a
polynomial of degree at most $d$, then for every finite set $A$ of nonzero field
elements with $d+1\le |A|$, the reconstruction sum using the Lagrange coefficients for
$A$ and the shares $f(i)$ equals $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Additivity of Recombination]
\lean{TCSlib.Shamir.recombine_add}
\label{TCSlib.Shamir.recombine_add}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.Shamir.Party, TCSlib.Shamir.recombine}
\difficulty{1}
Let $F$ be a field, let $A$ be a finite set of nonzero elements of $F$, and let $f,g$
assign field elements to each nonzero element of $F$. Recombination from $A$ is
additive: recombining $f+g$ gives the sum of the recombinations of $f$ and $g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Homogeneity of Recombination]
\lean{TCSlib.Shamir.recombine_smul}
\label{TCSlib.Shamir.recombine_smul}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.Shamir.Party, TCSlib.Shamir.recombine}
\difficulty{3}
Let $F$ be a field, let $A$ be a finite set of nonzero elements of $F$, let $c\in F$,
and let $f$ assign a field element to each nonzero element of $F$. Recombining the
values $c f(i)$ from $A$ equals $c$ times the recombination of $f$ from $A$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Linearity of reconstruction]
\lean{TCSlib.Shamir.recombine_sum}
\label{TCSlib.Shamir.recombine_sum}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.Shamir.Party, TCSlib.Shamir.recombine}
\difficulty{3}
Let $F$ be a field, let $A$ be a finite set of nonzero elements of $F$, and let $s$ be a
finite index set. For any family of shares $h_i(a)\in F$ indexed by $i\in s$ and $a\in
A$, reconstructing the pointwise sum of the shares gives the sum of their
reconstructions: $\operatorname{recombine}_A\bigl(a\mapsto\sum_{i\in
s}h_i(a)\bigr)=\sum_{i\in s}\operatorname{recombine}_A(h_i)$, where reconstruction uses
the Lagrange interpolation coefficients at $0$.
\end{theorem}
